why: Take 1 has the cleanest order and a true, ordinary shift line. Its gaps close with lifts from takes 2 and 3. It holds to the capstone [d8719fcc42e7edb421793dc5]: she calls him, tells him someone knows and looked suspicious, and he runs back.
changes: Fixer's opening lifted from take 3, so 'and nothing else' sets up the word she then breaks. Inez's reply now gives way fast and shows her fear as a question, replacing the tables excuse.
Okafor's 'That's not your voice' lifted from take 2, replacing 'ringing the door', so his question makes her next line necessary and only he could say it.
'Then it's bad' became 'It's only a door', which shows he likes her more than the job and turns on him when he runs back to it.
Cut 'See to your tables' from his last line; 'my door's standing empty' now says plainly what her word has done, with no time given. Learned line reworded to name Okafor.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: It's time, Inez. Okafor hears what we agreed, and nothing else.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Yes, I'll call him. Did anyone hear you ask for me?

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: It's me, love. Have they stamped your shift card yet?

beats.speaker: Okafor
beats.line: Not till the change. That's not your voice. What is it?

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: I've something to tell you that can't wait. Not on the line.

beats.speaker: Okafor
beats.line: It's only a door. All right, I'm off it.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Someone knows about us, love. Whoever it was looked suspicious.

beats.speaker: Okafor
beats.line: And my door's standing empty. I'm running back to it, now.

learned: Okafor warned: door empty less time.
opens: Enforcer can still Enter the Office.
